plan.title: Fix Windows deft-hook bin wiring and move ps1 cleanup to the launcher

narratives.Description: Global deft-hook still points at a POSIX /bin/sh shim, so Windows cmd/pwsh cannot run the registered hook and doctor reports spawn-failed. Separately, runtime postinstall still owns #4654 ps1 cleanup with a stale bin list, which breaks pnpm strict-dep-builds.
narratives.ImplementationPlan:
1. Point packages/cli package.json bin.deft-hook at a Node/dist entry (and packages/cli/bin/deft-hook[.cmd] as needed) so Windows cmd/pwsh starts Node rather than a POSIX /bin/sh shim, and align doctor live-probe with the registered host command.
2. Move Windows .ps1 shim cleanup into the launcher postinstall with correct PACKAGE_BIN_NAMES in packages/runtime/src/windows-bin-ps1.ts, no-op or remove the runtime postinstall owner, and extend windows-bin-ps1.test.ts fixtures to assert cleanup and that pnpm strict-dep-builds no longer fail.
narratives.UserStory: As a Windows OVPR consumer, I want deft-hook and doctor probe to work from cmd/pwsh after install, so that hooks activate without spawn-failed noise.

narrative.Acceptance: Given a Windows-like bin install of @deftai/directive, when deft-hook is invoked via the registered bin entry, then it starts Node rather than a POSIX /bin/sh shim.

Given launcher postinstall runs with the correct PACKAGE_BIN_NAMES, when runtime is installed under pnpm strict-dep-builds, then runtime postinstall does not fail the install and stale .ps1 shims for Directive bins are cleaned from the launcher path.

expected_outputs: windows-bin-ps1 tests pass; bin/package.json wiring reviewed for Windows entry
